display.purpose: The one headline at the top of a surface, in narrow capitals.

title.purpose: A document's own title and result headings.

body.purpose: Redline's explanations, at most 62 characters per line.

body-small.purpose: Fine print, field hints and the letterhead link.

document.purpose: The text of the document being read, in the Georgia-width serif.

document-quote.purpose: A single source sentence shown large with its film.

label.purpose: Tab labels, clause numbers, form labels.

shadows.name: sheet-shadow
shadows.purpose: Every sheet and every flag note: paper resting on the desk.

shadows.name: sheet-edge
shadows.purpose: The visible paper edge on the right of sheets that carry tabs; paired with the sheet shadow.

shadows.name: tab-shadow
shadows.purpose: Every tab: film lifted slightly off the paper.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Fast-then-gentle curve for the tab entrance, film tint and note slide.

motion.name: tab-stick
motion.value: 560ms ease-out-quart; from translateX(32px) and opacity 0; delay 350ms + rank x 160ms
motion.purpose: Tabs sticking on one at a time in rank order, once per page load.

motion.name: film-tint
motion.purpose: A sentence's film deepening when its flag is chosen.

motion.name: note-follow
motion.purpose: The open note sliding to stay level with its tab.

motion.name: tab-nudge
motion.value: transform 200ms ease-out; 4px on hover, 6px when chosen
motion.purpose: A tab moving toward the sheet, or the forward tab moving toward where it leads.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Entrance, film transition and note slide are all switched off.

narrative.overview:
Every Redline screen is one white printed sheet lying on a cool grey desk. The document being read is the sheet. When something in it matters, a coloured adhesive tab is stuck beside the exact sentence, the way a contract arrives from a lawyer marked "sign here". The tab is see-through film, so the sentence it marks is tinted in the same colour. Red tabs mark must-change flags. Yellow tabs mark worth-raising flags. Ballpoint blue is the reader's own pen, and appears only where the reader acts.

The world is quiet and literal. Text sits on paper at a comfortable reading size, with wide margins. Depth comes from paper resting on a desk: soft shadows, a thin visible paper edge on the right, and tabs that stick out past that edge onto the grey. Contract text is set in a serif that matches Georgia's letter widths, because that is how emailed agreements usually print. Everything Redline itself says (headings, tab labels, controls) is set in narrow, heavy capitals, like the print on a stationery tab.

Motion is spare. On first load the tabs stick on one at a time in rank order, sliding in from the right and settling. After that, only tab state changes move: a tab nudges toward the sheet when chosen, its sentence's tint deepens, and its note slides level with it. Nothing else animates.
keyCharacteristics: One sheet per surface, square-cornered, on a grey desk.
Tabs are the only strong colour, and colour always means severity (red or yellow) or the reader's own action (blue).
A tab is always attached to something: a sentence, a row, or an action.
Two voices: a Georgia-like serif for the document, condensed capitals for Redline.
One entrance animation, then only state changes.

rules.name: The Colour Means Severity Rule
rules.body: Red and yellow appear only as tabs and their film, and they always mean must-change and worth-raising. The red forward tab for the main action is the single exception, because it is still a tab. Never use red or yellow for decoration, warnings unrelated to a flag, or emphasis.

rules.name: The Reader's Pen Rule
rules.body: Ballpoint blue marks only the reader's own actions: links, focus rings and the text cursor. Redline's own voice never writes in blue.

rules.name: The Film Contrast Rule
rules.body: Tab colours are chosen so labels keep at least 4.5 to 1 contrast (the minimum readable ratio for small text) over both the sheet and the desk. Red tabs take off-white labels; yellow tabs take black ones.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The document is always in the serif. Redline is always in Archivo. A source sentence quoted anywhere, including inside a note, keeps the serif so it reads as the document's own words.

rules.name: The Printed Caps Rule
rules.body: Narrow capitals are for headings, tab labels, controls and short captions only. Never set a sentence of explanation in them.

rules.name: The Sheet Is The Page Rule
rules.body: A surface is a sheet on a desk, never a dashboard of panels. When the signed-in app is built, the document stays the sheet, the margin column to its right becomes the working column (the selected flag's note, then the question box), and any navigation is a narrow strip on the left of the desk, not a second sheet.

rules.name: The Two Layers Rule
rules.body: Paper sits on the desk; film sits on the paper. A note is a second slip of paper and takes the sheet shadow. There is no third, higher layer, and no pop-up windows.

dos: Do put every surface on a Laser Paper sheet (#fbfcfc) resting on the Cool Grey Desk (#d3d7dc), with square corners and the sheet shadow.
Do attach every tab to the exact sentence or row it marks, pointed end toward it, sticking out past the sheet's right edge.
Do tint the source sentence with the film of its tab's colour, and deepen the film when the flag is chosen.
Do set document text, and any quote from it, in Gelasio at a comfortable reading size.
Do keep Ballpoint Blue (#1f3a93) for links, focus rings and the text cursor only.
Do keep motion to the single tab entrance and tab state changes, and switch both off when the reader's device asks for reduced motion.
donts: Don't use red or yellow for anything but a tab, its film, or the forward action tab.
Don't draw a rounded card, a bordered box or a pill as a container or a button. A container is a sheet or a slip of paper; a button is a tab.
Don't use gradients, icons or illustrations to stand in for a tab or a flag.
Don't add a hard, solid offset shadow, or any shadow stronger than the sheet shadow.
Don't set Redline's explanations in the serif, or the document's words in Archivo.
Don't show a tab whose source sentence is not on the sheet.
